creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Every pane of the 0.3.0 cask renders nothing, and says so:

    muster-bridge: could not start herdr: No such file or directory (os error 2)

`herdr_binary()` looks for a file called `herdr` beside the bridge's own executable, and falls back to PATH (`crates/muster-bridge/src/main.rs:258-266`). `1d7ace3` moved the daemon into `Contents/Library/MusterSessions.app/` and dropped the `cp` that put a copy in `Contents/MacOS/`, so a released bundle has no herdr beside its bridge: `Contents/MacOS/` holds the three muster binaries and nothing else.

The PATH fallback cannot save it, which is the part worth knowing. libghostty spawns the bridge, so the bridge inherits the *app's* environment rather than the daemon's - and an app opened by Launch Services gets launchd's `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, read off the running process. Every directory on it is SIP-protected, so there is nowhere to put a herdr even deliberately, and the `~/.muster/bin` the daemon puts on a *pane's* PATH never reaches the bridge.

`1d7ace3` is an ancestor of the 0.3.0 commit, so every `brew install amterp/tap/muster` since the release opens a window where no pane renders.

A dev build hides it. `./dev` stages herdr beside the bridge in the SwiftPM bin directory (`dev:497-498`), which is the one layout the "beside me" rule is right about, and `tools/smoke-launch.py` launches `.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/muster` - so the contract tier never sees a bundle either.

Verified on a work laptop, clean cask install. The workaround that survives a normal launch is a symlink where the bridge already looks - `ln -s ../Library/MusterSessions.app/Contents/MacOS/herdr /Applications/Muster.app/Contents/MacOS/herdr` - after which a Dock launch renders and `pgrep` shows the bridge running its `herdr terminal session control`. It costs the bundle its seal, `codesign --verify` then reporting a missing sealed resource, and the app opens anyway because it was approved before the edit; a `brew upgrade` takes the symlink away again. Setting the app's PATH instead - `open -a Muster --env "PATH=$HOME/.muster/bin:..."` - works for that one launch and no other, which is the point: somebody opening Muster from the Dock cannot reach the fallback at all.

So the fix has to hand the bridge a path. The app already resolves the daemon in `HerdrLocation.swift`, and passing it as `--herdr-binary` beside the `--herdr-socket` it already passes keeps the rule in one place - the argument the bridge's own comment on `herdr_socket` makes. The alternative is teaching the bridge the bundle layout, beside then `../Library/MusterSessions.app/Contents/MacOS/herdr`, which is smaller but puts that path in a second file. Keep the PATH fallback either way for a bridge run by hand; just do not count on it.

Whichever it is, it wants a check that runs against an assembled bundle. Nothing in the suite launches one today, which is why this reached a release.

## Reproducing it

1. Install the cask - `brew install amterp/tap/muster` at 0.3.0, or assemble any bundle built after `1d7ace3` - and launch it from the Dock, Finder or Spotlight.
2. Every pane prints the ENOENT and Ghostty's `Process exited`.
3. The two facts behind it, checkable without launching anything:

       ls /Applications/Muster.app/Contents/MacOS      # muster, muster-bridge, muster-cli - no herdr
       ps eww -p $(pgrep -f 'Muster.app/Contents/MacOS/muster$') | tr ' ' '\n' | grep ^PATH=
       # PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin - launchd's, and every entry is SIP-protected

4. The run log records it as `bridge.herdr.failed` per pane.

It matters that the app is launched the normal way. `open -a Muster --env "PATH=$HOME/.muster/bin:$PATH"` with a herdr on that PATH renders fine, which is a useful A/B but not a state any user is in.

## Validating a fix

- A Dock-launched cask build renders every pane, and `pgrep -fl 'herdr terminal session control'` shows one client per pane.
- `codesign --verify --strict /Applications/Muster.app` still passes - whatever the fix is, it must not need a file added to a signed bundle by hand, which is what the workaround does.
- The check that would have caught it has to run against an *assembled bundle*: `tools/smoke-launch.py` launches `.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/muster`, where herdr sits beside the bridge and the bug cannot appear. Pointing a launch check at `Muster.app` is the regression test.
title: 📦 A brew-installed 0.3.0 renders nothing in every pane
